status_effects.explanation: Accused by Odette and consequently shunned outright by Swann (refused handshake), oncle Adolphe moves from trusted family confidant to a broken relation within this local episode.

Charlus is affirmed as a trusted intimate included in Swann's confidence, though the scene's manipulative undertone (Swann feigning confusion to extract more detail) tempers how purely genuine this warmth is.

appraisal_events.evidence: Odette disait à Swann qu'elle venait d'avoir une déception en voyant que mon oncle était pareil à tous les hommes : il venait d'essayer de la prendre de force... il refusa de lui serrer la main quand il le rencontra.
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette's accusation that oncle Adolphe tried to force himself on her leads Swann to break with him, refusing to shake his hand; the narration never confirms whether the accusation is true, but the resulting local rupture is unambiguous.

appraisal_events.evidence: Swann savait qu'il ne pouvait rien se passer... c'était par amitié pour lui... « Vous êtes gentil, mon petit Mémé, je vous aime bien. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann trusts Charlus completely as a harmless, loyal companion for Odette and thanks him warmly, though the affection is entangled with Swann's strategic effort to draw out more information.

ambiguities: It is unclear whether oncle Adolphe actually attempted to force himself on Odette or whether her account is a pretext; this reaches the reader only via Odette's telling and is never independently confirmed, though the local social effect on oncle Adolphe (Swann's refusal to shake his hand) is unambiguous.
